entity.title: Note
entity.description: A supplemental explanation attached to a specific rule, providing clarification, context, or elaboration.

rules.body: IS associated with a single rule and must reference the rule's identifier explicitly (e.g., [<rule id>/<incremental note id (OOn)]).
A Note provides clarification, context, or elaboration and must not modify the rule it supplements.
MUST be stored in the same directory as the entity and rule it references.
MAY include: Business rationale, Examples or use cases, Historical context, Clarifications of terminology.
MUST be versioned and maintained alongside the rules they support.
MUST be concise but may span multiple paragraphs if needed for clarity.

Notes of type `supersedes`, `extends`, or `related` MUST reference rules by identifier `<EUID>-NNN`, or outside the Realm tree by `<realm-id>:<EUID>-NNN` naming a declared dependency or one of its sub-realms.
HAS a revision that is 0 when the Note is added and increments by one on each change to its content or type.
MUST NOT be removed once added.
Notes of type changelog, supersedes, extends or related MUST NOT change once added.
Note identifiers under a Rule MUST be sequential from 01.

A Note of type `extends` on a Rule that is not Abandoned, Retired or Terminated MUST NOT reference a Rule whose Entity has a visibility that does not permit inheritance from the Realm of the Note or that is narrower than the visibility of the Entity holding the Note.

A Note of type `standard` IS a mapping of its Rule to one clause of a standard, with content `<id>:<clause>` split at the first colon, where `<id>` is the `id` of a Standard Reference and `<clause>` is not blank.
A Rule MUST NOT hold two Notes of type `standard` with the same content.

The `<id>` of a `standard` Note MUST match a Standard Reference declared by the Entity owning the Rule, its containing Entities nearest first, its Realm or that Realm's parent, the first of these that declares it taking precedence.
A Note of type `standard` MAY be added, revised or retyped between that type and `reference` in any state of its Rule, and doing so leaves the revision of the Rule unchanged.
A mapping MUST be withdrawn only by changing its Note to type `reference` with its content unchanged.

notes.content: Versioned means two things. First, a Note is part of the hashed Rule Set of the Entity that holds it (RSTHSH-001), so adding or changing a Note bumps that Entity's rule_set version (patch), timestamp and hash, and the change is reviewed through strspc diff like any Rule change. Second, each Note carries its own revision (NTE-008) that counts changes to its content or type. Notes are never removed (NTE-009): a Note that no longer applies is revised in place, except that Notes of the append-only types never change at all (NTE-010). Note identifiers under a Rule stay sequential (NTE-011), and because a Note is never removed an identifier is never reused.

Before this rule, a Note's revision recorded the revision of the referenced Rule at the time the Note was added. Nothing read or checked that value, it was 0 on almost every Note because Rule revisions rarely move, and it gave no way to tell that a Note's content had changed. Redefining it as the Note's own edit counter mirrors a Rule's revision: a content change without a revision increment is a diff error, so every edit is visible in review. Notes are never removed (NTE-009), so identifiers under a Rule stay sequential (NTE-011) and no history is needed to prevent their reuse; a stale Note is revised in place unless it is of an append-only type (NTE-010).

A mapping is a claim about a Rule and does not change what the Rule requires, so it stays a Note and RUL-007 is not engaged. A Rule field would need superseding every mapped Rule when a standard is renumbered in a new edition.
NTE-009 forbids removing a Note, and NTE-011 keeps Note identifiers sequential. A `reference` Note stays out of the evaluator prompt and out of coverage, and keeps the record of the mapping.
